newsitem.title: GREECE: BANK/GREECE WANTS INFLATION BELOW 3 PCT BY END-98.
newsitem.headline: BANK/GREECE WANTS INFLATION BELOW 3 PCT BY END-98.

text.p: The main goal of Greek monetary policy is to slash inflation to 4.5 percent by end-1997 and below 3.0 percent by end-98, central bank governor Lucas Papademos said on Friday.

"The strategy of the central bank for reducing inflation to 4.5 percent by end-97 and below 3.0 percent by end-98, in line with the government's target, will be similar to that followed in the previous two years," Papademos told a news conference.

Greek headline CPI inflation fell to 7.5 percent year-on-year in December 1996 from 7.7 percent in November and 8.1 percent at end-95. Average inflation stood at 8.5 percent in 1996 versus 9.3 percent in 1995.
"What is important is not the short-term fluctuations of inflation but the course of core inflation in the medium term," said Papademos.
He expressed optimism that inflation would stay on a downward course in the next few months reflecting an easing of inflationary pressures .

But central bank figures showed that underlying or core inflation which does not include volatile food and energy prices was stable to firm in the last four months of 1996, rising to 8.2 percent year-on-year in December, from 8.0 percent in November.

He added that lower inflation was "a neccesary but not a sufficient condition" to achieve faster economic growth and pointed out that Greece had succeeded in cutting inflation while speeding up GDP growth in the last few years.
Greek GDP growth is projected at 3.3 percent in 1997 from an expected 2.6 percent in 1996, based on national economy estimates.

"The strategy ...will be based on two intermediate targets to attain the final goal (slashing inflation): The stability of the foreign exchange rate of the drachma and the slowdown of monetary expansion within limits compatible with the desired reduction of inflation," said Papademos.
He said the general framework of conducting monetary policy will be stable but there will be changes in the way intermediate targets are set.
Policy tools will also be adjusted to take into consideration inflation and prevailing conditions in the money and forex markets.
The Bank of Greece uses M3, credit expansion and ecu/drachma targeting to meet its end-year inflation goals.
